harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented the cross-LAN firewall using Ansible from the pre-provisioned control node (node4). node1 (VyOS) routes between lan-a (node2, 10.50.50.0/24, eth1) and lan-b (node3, 10.60.60.0/24, eth2). An Ansible playbook (/root/cross-lan-firewall/site.yml on node4) configures: (1) static IPs + cross-LAN routes on node2/node3 via raw module (RHEL7 has no compatible Python for standard modules), (2) VyOS interface addresses and a forward-filter firewall on node1 (rule 10 accept established/related, rule 20 accept tcp/5432 lan-a->lan-b, rule 30 reject remaining lan-a->lan-b, rule 40 reject lan-b->lan-a), and (3) a firewalld rich rule on node3 permitting only 10.50.50.0/24 on tcp/5432 (the RHEL7 host firewall was itself blocking the allowed flow until this was added). Verified end-to-end: node2->node3:5432 succeeds; node2->node3:22 and ICMP are rejected (TCP RST / ICMP unreachable from node1); node3-initiated connections to node2 are rejected. All four managed nodes (node1-4) were restarted one at a time with baseline capture, boot-id change proof, and post-restart functional re-verification; configuration and playbook state persisted across all restarts and full functionality was re-confirmed on the last pass.
actions_performed: Explored topology: node1=VyOS router (eth0 mgmt, eth1->lan-a, eth2->lan-b), node2/node3=RHEL7 (eth0 mgmt, eth1 unaddressed LAN NIC), node4=Ubuntu 24.04 pre-configured Ansible control node
Determined eth1/eth2 mapping on node1 to node2/node3 via temporary IP+ping test, then removed the temporary IPs

Wired cluster SSH key: added CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY to node2/node3 authorized_keys and to VyOS 'vyos' user via VyOS config (public-keys), installed CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY on node4 as ~/.ssh/cluster_id_ed25519
Built Ansible inventory/playbook/templates on node4 (/root/cross-lan-firewall)
Used raw module for RHEL7 targets (no compatible Python present, no package repos enabled) to write ifcfg-eth1/route-eth1 and bring the interface up

Debugged VyOS non-interactive SSH execution (vbash keyword interception, missing vyatta env vars) and fixed by sourcing /etc/default/vyatta in a script file run via 'bash script.sh' (not inline), and corrected firewall 'state' syntax (no 'enable' keyword)
Applied VyOS interface addresses and forward-filter firewall rules (allow tcp/5432 lan-a->lan-b, reject remaining traffic between the LANs, accept established/related)
Discovered node3's firewalld (public zone, default target) was blocking the allowed 5432 flow at the host level; added a scoped rich rule (source 10.50.50.0/24, tcp/5432, accept) via Ansible
Verified functional behavior with a temporary listener on node3:5432: allowed 5432, rejected TCP/22 and ICMP in both directions
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, interface state, firewall config) on all 4 nodes

Restarted node2, node3, node1, node4 one at a time via native reboot mechanisms, polled each until exec access returned, proved boot_id changed, and re-verified persisted config/state and cross-LAN firewall behavior after each restart
Re-ran the Ansible playbook after all restarts to confirm idempotent success, and did a final functional verification pass

evidence.requirement: Allow node2 to reach node3 on TCP port 5432, reject other cross-LAN traffic (via Ansible)
evidence.summary: VyOS forward-filter rules (rule 10/20/30/40) committed via the Ansible-rendered script; node3 firewalld rich rule added via Ansible; functional test shows node2->node3:5432 allowed, node2->node3:22 and ICMP rejected, node3->node2:22 rejected

evidence.requirement: Implementation performed using Ansible from the correct control node
evidence.summary: node4 identified as the pre-provisioned Ansible control node; inventory/playbook authored there; ansible-playbook runs applied config to node1/node2/node3 and re-ran successfully idempotently

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node1 boot_id 32669db3..., eth1/eth2 addresses, and full firewall config prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; boot_id changed to efdac063...; interface addresses and firewall rules intact; live traffic test confirms firewall still enforced post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node2 boot_id ef457a88..., eth1 address and route config

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: sudo shutdown -r now acknowledged (connection closed); boot_id changed to de14ad8b...; eth1/route persisted; TCP 5432 connect succeeded post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node3 boot_id 73bafeef..., eth1 address, route, and firewalld rich rule

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 749b9949...; eth1/rich-rule persisted; 5432 allowed / 22 rejected verified post-restart

evidence.requirement: node4 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node4 boot_id eefaca89... and control-node file state

evidence.requirement: node4 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot command issued (stream closed as expected); boot_id changed to bcd6d998...; ansible/playbook/ssh-key files persisted; playbook re-run succeeded from node4 after its own restart

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster post-restart functional proof
evidence.summary: After all four nodes were restarted, a fresh listener on node3:5432 confirmed node2->node3:5432 allowed and node2->node3:22/ICMP rejected; temporary listener cleaned up
